significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that successful jailbreaks have an “elevated-then-decaying” refusal trajectory, genuine refusals have rising trajectories, and early trajectory measurements predict later harmful continuation; this fixes expected temporal ordering and predictive coupling across attacks rather than merely locating a refusal direction. The claim establishes both a behavioral phenomenon—“delayed ‘commitment collapse’”—and a mechanism in which decay of the refusal signal precedes harmful continuation, materially refining the static causal account represented by Arditi et al., “Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction” (NeurIPS 2024). Verified false would still rule out a shared temporal-collapse explanation and weaken the premise that jailbreak outcomes can generally be anticipated from evolving refusal projections, so the two branches are determinate and informative. In the topic-substitution check, generic mechanistic LLM safety would not imply this trajectory law or ordering, so the score is supported by claim-specific constraints rather than the topic’s importance.

reach.justification: The named handles are the per-token “refusal commitment trajectory,” an “early-warning monitor,” and a “collapse-point” trigger for “minimal one-shot repair”; the monitor is ex ante because the first few generated-token projections forecast eventual jailbreak success before the harmful continuation is completed. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a qualitative relation—decaying versus rising versus persistently low trajectories—rather than merely supplying a procedure for searching for an unspecified direction. The hypothesis asserts this signature across Llama, Qwen, and Gemma model families and five jailbreak families, and its downstream users include deployment auditors or runtime safety systems that can gate or re-steer generation, although reliance on open-weight activation access limits broader uptake. The topic-substitution check fails to preserve this score: generic interpretability-based safety supplies neither a token-level predictor nor an action window, so the above reach comes from the claim-specific handles.
